request.system:
You explain a fitted credit-risk model to a credit risk manager who is not a data scientist. You receive the facts about one model and write a short explanation of what drives its predictions of default.

# The text

- Write 5 to 8 sentences in plain English, most important drivers first.
- Mention an interaction when it matters for the model's predictions.
- Say only what the facts support. Do not round a weak effect up to a strong one, and do not add knowledge about credit risk that the facts do not show.
- When the facts do not settle something, say so ("the data do not settle whether ...") or leave it out.

# The answer

Return one JSON object with one list, `sentences`, each with an `id` (1, 2, 3, ...) and its `text`.
messages:
These are the facts about the model.

Model: a gradient-boosted tree model of depth 2 (XGB2), fitted to predict whether a credit applicant defaults (30,000 applicants). Effects are on the log-odds scale: positive values raise the risk of default. Every band is a 95% band from 100 refits of the model on resampled data.

Features, in the order of their share of the model's importance:
- `PAY_0`: repayment status in September 2005, the latest month (-1 paid in full, 1 to 9 months of payment delay; -2 and 0 are not in the data dictionary, commonly read as no consumption and revolving credit used).
  Share of importance 25.3% (95% band 22.8% to 31.0%); rank 1 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= -1: -0.1; 0: -0.5; 1: +0.7; >= 2: +2 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +2.11, 95% band [+1.94, +2.28]).
- `LIMIT_BAL`: amount of the given credit in NT dollars, individual and family (supplementary) credit.
  Share of importance 14.7% (95% band 13.2% to 17.4%); rank 2 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= 49999: +0.7; 50000-149999: +0.207; >= 150000: -0.34 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -1.14, 95% band [-1.39, -0.93]).
- `PAY_AMT1`: amount paid in September 2005, the latest month, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 8.9% (95% band 6.4% to 10.2%); rank 3 to 4 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= 2355: +0.18; >= 2356: -0.2 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.63, 95% band [-0.82, -0.42]).
- `BILL_AMT1`: amount of the bill statement in September 2005, the latest month, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 7.0% (95% band 3.3% to 8.7%); rank 3 to 6 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= 21952: -0.15; >= 21953: +0.1 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.67, 95% band [+0.25, +0.89]).
- `PAY_AMT2`: amount paid in August 2005, the month before, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 5.3% (95% band 2.9% to 7.3%); rank 4 to 6 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= 24314: +0.01; >= 24315: -0.3 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.40, 95% band [-0.60, -0.16]).
- `BILL_AMT2`: amount of the bill statement in August 2005, the month before, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 3.2% (95% band 1.2% to 6.3%); rank 4 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): rises by 0.28 (95% band [+0.01, +0.49]) from x = 0 (5th percentile) to x = 195,000 (95th percentile); the shape in between is not resolved at this sample size.
- `AGE`: age in years.
  Share of importance 2.3% (95% band 1.6% to 3.7%); rank 6 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): rises by 0.21 (95% band [+0.06, +0.39]) from x = 23 (5th percentile) to x = 53 (95th percentile); the shape in between is not resolved at this sample size.
- `PAY_AMT3`: amount paid in July 2005, two months before, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 2.3% (95% band 0.5% to 3.4%); rank 5 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.15, 95% band [-0.04, +0.28]).
- `EDUCATION`: education (1 graduate school, 2 university, 3 high school, 4 others; 0, 5 and 6 are not in the data dictionary).
  Share of importance 1.3% (95% band 0.8% to 3.9%); rank 5 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): rises by 0.08 (95% band [+0.03, +0.28]) from x = 1 (5th percentile) to x = 3 (95th percentile); the shape in between is not resolved at this sample size.

Interactions: the model has 36 pairs. The larger ones:
- `PAY_0 & EDUCATION`: share of importance 10.7% (95% band 8.2% to 14.1%).
  Effect of `PAY_0` from -2 to 2: +1.50 (95% band +1.32 to +1.73) when `EDUCATION` = 1, +4.10 (95% band +3.72 to +4.85) when `EDUCATION` = 3.
  Effect of `EDUCATION` from 1 to 3: -0.24 (95% band -0.46 to -0.02) when `PAY_0` = -2, +2.36 (95% band +1.98 to +3.12) when `PAY_0` = 2.
- `BILL_AMT1 & AGE`: share of importance 3.1% (95% band 0.4% to 3.1%).
  Effect of `BILL_AMT1` from 0 to 201,000: +0.99 (95% band +0.34 to +1.21) when `AGE` = 23, +0.20 (95% band -0.02 to +0.57) when `AGE` = 53.
  Effect of `AGE` from 23 to 53: +0.57 (95% band +0.08 to +0.74) when `BILL_AMT1` = 0, -0.22 (95% band -0.40 to +0.21) when `BILL_AMT1` = 201,000.
- `PAY_AMT1 & AGE`: share of importance 1.3% (95% band 0.3% to 2.1%).
  Effect of `PAY_AMT1` from 0 to 18,400: -0.57 (95% band -0.78 to -0.37) when `AGE` = 23, -0.84 (95% band -1.05 to -0.50) when `AGE` = 53.
  Effect of `AGE` from 23 to 53: +0.31 (95% band +0.11 to +0.53) when `PAY_AMT1` = 0, +0.04 (95% band -0.12 to +0.29) when `PAY_AMT1` = 18,400.
- `PAY_0 & AGE`: share of importance 1.2% (95% band 0.2% to 2.4%).
  Effect of `PAY_0` from -2 to 2: +2.15 (95% band +1.98 to +2.37) when `AGE` = 23, +2.22 (95% band +1.90 to +2.29) when `AGE` = 53.
  Effect of `AGE` from 23 to 53: +0.27 (95% band +0.12 to +0.52) when `PAY_0` = -2, +0.34 (95% band +0.02 to +0.47) when `PAY_0` = 2.
- `PAY_0 & LIMIT_BAL`: share of importance 1.1% (95% band 0.7% to 1.9%).
  Effect of `PAY_0` from -2 to 2: +1.94 (95% band +1.67 to +2.13) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 20,000, +2.19 (95% band +1.94 to +2.45) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 430,000.
  Effect of `LIMIT_BAL` from 20,000 to 430,000: -1.26 (95% band -1.57 to -0.98) when `PAY_0` = -2, -1.02 (95% band -1.22 to -0.67) when `PAY_0` = 2.
- `LIMIT_BAL & PAY_AMT1`: share of importance 0.9% (95% band 0.3% to 1.6%).
  Effect of `LIMIT_BAL` from 20,000 to 430,000: -1.04 (95% band -1.41 to -0.84) when `PAY_AMT1` = 0, -1.24 (95% band -1.47 to -0.90) when `PAY_AMT1` = 18,400.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT1` from 0 to 18,400: -0.51 (95% band -0.85 to -0.34) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 20,000, -0.71 (95% band -0.90 to -0.39) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 430,000.
- `LIMIT_BAL & PAY_AMT2`: share of importance 0.9% (95% band 0.1% to 1.3%).
  Effect of `LIMIT_BAL` from 20,000 to 430,000: -1.16 (95% band -1.47 to -0.95) when `PAY_AMT2` = 0, -1.33 (95% band -1.45 to -0.89) when `PAY_AMT2` = 19,000.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT2` from 0 to 19,000: -0.39 (95% band -0.73 to -0.20) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 20,000, -0.55 (95% band -0.66 to -0.15) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 430,000.
- `PAY_AMT1 & BILL_AMT2`: share of importance 0.8% (95% band 0.1% to 1.4%).
  Effect of `PAY_AMT1` from 0 to 18,400: -0.58 (95% band -0.84 to +0.09) when `BILL_AMT2` = 0, -0.80 (95% band -1.26 to -0.49) when `BILL_AMT2` = 195,000.
  Effect of `BILL_AMT2` from 0 to 195,000: +0.45 (95% band +0.05 to +0.81) when `PAY_AMT1` = 0, +0.23 (95% band -0.53 to +0.44) when `PAY_AMT1` = 18,400.
- `PAY_AMT1 & EDUCATION`: share of importance 0.7% (95% band 0.3% to 1.8%).
  Effect of `PAY_AMT1` from 0 to 18,400: -0.61 (95% band -0.78 to -0.38) when `EDUCATION` = 1, -0.73 (95% band -1.01 to -0.53) when `EDUCATION` = 3.
  Effect of `EDUCATION` from 1 to 3: +0.20 (95% band +0.13 to +0.49) when `PAY_AMT1` = 0, +0.08 (95% band -0.03 to +0.30) when `PAY_AMT1` = 18,400.
- `PAY_AMT2 & EDUCATION`: share of importance 0.7% (95% band 0.0% to 0.9%).
  Effect of `PAY_AMT2` from 0 to 19,000: -0.38 (95% band -0.60 to -0.16) when `EDUCATION` = 1, -0.52 (95% band -0.63 to -0.16) when `EDUCATION` = 3.
  Effect of `EDUCATION` from 1 to 3: +0.18 (95% band +0.03 to +0.31) when `PAY_AMT2` = 0, +0.03 (95% band -0.00 to +0.30) when `PAY_AMT2` = 19,000.
- `PAY_AMT1 & PAY_AMT3`: share of importance 0.6% (95% band 0.0% to 1.3%).
  Effect of `PAY_AMT1` from 0 to 18,400: -0.71 (95% band -0.90 to -0.43) when `PAY_AMT3` = 0, -0.55 (95% band -0.82 to -0.39) when `PAY_AMT3` = 17,600.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT3` from 0 to 17,600: +0.11 (95% band -0.04 to +0.33) when `PAY_AMT1` = 0, +0.27 (95% band -0.03 to +0.39) when `PAY_AMT1` = 18,400.
- `BILL_AMT1 & PAY_AMT2`: share of importance 0.6% (95% band 0.1% to 1.0%).
  Effect of `BILL_AMT1` from 0 to 201,000: +0.61 (95% band +0.20 to +0.82) when `PAY_AMT2` = 0, +0.73 (95% band +0.27 to +0.93) when `PAY_AMT2` = 19,000.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT2` from 0 to 19,000: -0.41 (95% band -0.69 to -0.17) when `BILL_AMT1` = 0, -0.29 (95% band -0.51 to -0.10) when `BILL_AMT1` = 201,000.
- `PAY_0 & BILL_AMT1`: share of importance 0.6% (95% band 0.1% to 0.8%).
  Effect of `PAY_0` from -2 to 2: +2.19 (95% band +1.92 to +2.35) when `BILL_AMT1` = 0, +2.07 (95% band +1.75 to +2.29) when `BILL_AMT1` = 201,000.
  Effect of `BILL_AMT1` from 0 to 201,000: +0.73 (95% band +0.24 to +1.06) when `PAY_0` = -2, +0.61 (95% band +0.26 to +0.89) when `PAY_0` = 2.

  Effect of `BILL_AMT1` from 0 to 201,000: +0.85 (95% band +0.28 to +1.14) when `PAY_AMT1` = 0, +0.53 (95% band +0.22 to +0.87) when `PAY_AMT1` = 18,400.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT1` from 0 to 18,400: -0.47 (95% band -0.80 to -0.36) when `BILL_AMT1` = 0, -0.79 (95% band -1.06 to -0.44) when `BILL_AMT1` = 201,000.

  Effect of `PAY_AMT2` from 0 to 19,000: -0.39 (95% band -0.56 to -0.12) when `AGE` = 23, -0.48 (95% band -0.81 to -0.21) when `AGE` = 53.
  Effect of `AGE` from 23 to 53: +0.24 (95% band +0.07 to +0.47) when `PAY_AMT2` = 0, +0.16 (95% band -0.08 to +0.36) when `PAY_AMT2` = 19,000.
- `LIMIT_BAL & AGE`: share of importance 0.5% (95% band 0.3% to 1.3%).
  Effect of `LIMIT_BAL` from 20,000 to 430,000: -1.08 (95% band -1.37 to -0.75) when `AGE` = 23, -1.23 (95% band -1.60 to -0.95) when `AGE` = 53.
  Effect of `AGE` from 23 to 53: +0.31 (95% band +0.11 to +0.53) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 20,000, +0.16 (95% band -0.09 to +0.34) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 430,000.
- 20 further pairs with a share below 0.5% each, together 4.9%.

Write the explanation.

content.text: {"sentences":[{"id":1,"text":"The model's predictions of default are driven mainly by repayment status in the latest month (September 2005), which accounts for about a quarter of the model's importance; a delay of two or more months raises the predicted risk by roughly 2 units on the log-odds scale, while being paid in full lowers it slightly."},{"id":2,"text":"The credit limit (LIMIT_BAL) is the second most important driver: applicants with limits under 50,000 NT dollars carry higher predicted risk, and risk falls as the limit rises, with the net drop from low to high limits about 1.1 log-odds units."},{"id":3,"text":"The amount paid in September 2005 is the third most important driver: payments of about 2,356 NT dollars or more lower predicted risk, with a net effect of roughly -0.6 across the typical range."},{"id":4,"text":"The effects of repayment status and education interact strongly: the effect of repayment status is much larger for applicants with education level 3 (high school) than for those with education level 1 (graduate school), so the two cannot be read separately."},{"id":5,"text":"Several other variables matter less: the September bill amount, the August payment and bill amount, and age each add or subtract modest amounts, and the data do not clearly resolve the shape of their effects between the extremes."},{"id":6,"text":"The July payment amount and education level have small importance, and the data do not clearly show any movement from the July payment amount, so it should not be relied on as a driver."},{"id":7,"text":"Several pairwise interactions, such as between credit limit and payment amounts, are real but small, and the wide uncertainty bands on most of them mean their exact size should be treated with caution."}]}
